I was fully prepared for "Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia" to be a beautifully animated but straightforward historical piece. When you look at the soft, almost children's book aesthetic, it's easy to assume this will be a gentle story. But don't let the fluffy character designs fool you. Underneath its harmless exterior, this series hides a story about war, conquest, slavery, and political assassination, proving that allowing ugly things to exist within beautiful art only makes them hit harder.

In this video, we look into why this historical anime is so effective: the harrowing realities of former slave Sitara's quest for revenge against the Mongolian Empire, the immense complexity of the imperial court, and the brilliant subversion of a flawed protagonist who incorrectly assumes she is
title: This Anime Looks Cute. It Is Not.
